title: Autoscale playbook + mini-dashboard wireframes and grooming notes
content:
Purpose
This is a compact working doc: a UX-first playbook and a small set of annotated mini-dashboard wireframes for Dedicated capacity autoscale + burst/reservation controls. Goal is to provide a low-friction operator surface for: diagnose why a pool scaled, quickly change burst policy, and run immediate 'safe' overrides. Use this in grooming with SRE/serving-runtime and product to finalize scope for the next sprint.

High-level requirements (engineered from research + support tickets)
- Operators want a single glance view showing current pool utilization, recent automatic scale events, and the active reservation/burst rules that influenced scaling.
- Quick actions: pause autoscale, request burst (ad-hoc), convert burst to reservation, and surface rollback to previous replica set.
- Auditability: every manual override must record actor + reason and be visible in timeline.
- Safe defaults: UI should prevent misguided large-scale manual changes (confirm + estimated cost/latency impact shown).

Mini-dashboard concept (center-pane compact card)
- Card header: Pool name (clickable) | region tag | hardware profile (A100-80GB v2)
- Top-line KPIs (small chips): active shards, %gpu utilization (1m/5m), queued requests, mean tail latency (95p), token throughput
- Timeline bar: horizontal micro timeline (last 30m) with icons for: autoscale up, autoscale down, burst start, reservation start, manual override. Hover shows short tooltip: timestamp, triggering metric and brief causal note.
- Decision ribbon (below timeline): shows the rule evaluated at each decision point (e.g., "throughput > 120k tps -> scale +2") with color-coding: green=expected, amber=soft-fallback, red=forced/manual. Clicking an element opens side panel with details.

Wireframe annotations (quick ascii sketches)
- Top-left: Pool header + quick actions: [Pause autoscale] [Request burst] [Convert burst -> reservation] [Rollback last change]
- Center: Timeline band (scrollable horizontally) with markers
- Right-side: Decision side-panel (slides over, not nav) with 3 tabs: Summary | Logs & Traces | Cost estimate
- Bottom: Recent events table (last 100 events) with filters: source (autoscaler/runtime/operator), severity, ticket link.

Interaction flows (happy path)
1) Operator sees sudden latency spike and sees autoscaler scaled down 3m ago -> clicks the scale-down marker on timeline -> side-panel shows metrics that caused scale-down (low occupancy, underutilization) + option panels: [Revert scale-down] [Pause autoscale 15m] [Open quick-burst]
2) Operator selects [Quick-burst]: modal with presets (small/medium/large) shows estimated tokens served, estimated cost delta for next hr, and suggested scaling delta. Confirm requires reason text. On confirm the UI shows ephemeral 'optimistic state' while runtime processes the request and then updates timeline with burst-start marker.

Edge cases and guardrails
- If a manual burst request exceeds pool max reservation quota -> reject with remediation: suggest splitting across two pools or request support.
- If two operators attempt concurrent manual overrides, show last-writer-wins but show both entries in timeline and mark conflict in events table.
- Soft-fallback: if autoscaler cannot scale because of quota or hardware shortage, show an amber ribbon with suggested fallback models (lighter variant) and a one-click route to create a temporary ticket to ops.

Microcopy & labels (recommended)
- Pause autoscale -> "Pause autoscaling (temporary manual control). Autoscaler will be re-enabled automatically after X minutes unless reconfigured."
- Quick-burst -> "Request immediate burst capacity. This consumes burst quota and may affect cost. Provide brief rationale."
- Convert burst to reservation -> "Lock current realtime capacity as a reservation. This will consume reserved quota and may change billing."

Telemetry and metrics to expose from runtime (for the console)
- autoscaler_decision events (timestamp, triggered_by, current_replicas, target_replicas, reason_code)
- burst_request events (actor, preset, requested_replicas, granted_replicas, quota_consumed)
- reservation_change events (actor, duration, replicas)
- health heartbeats per host (GPU temp, mem, queue depth)
- cost_estimate snapshots (tokens_served_last_hour, estimated_cost_last_hour)

Acceptance criteria for initial implementation (MVP)
- Mini-dashboard card implemented in pool listing and pool detail pages (visual parity with wireframes).
- Timeline band shows up-to-date events with hover tooltips and click-to-open side panel.
- Quick-burst modal with at least two presets and cost estimate shown. Confirm writes burst_request event to audit log.
- Manual overrides require reason input and create an immutable audit entry.
- E2E: Operator can request quick burst and see the runtime grant event reflected within 30s in the UI.

Backlog grooming notes (estimated story points and owners)
- INF-3498: mini-dashboard card + timeline (5) - owner: Lara Morales
- INF-3509: quick-burst modal + presets (3) - owner: Tom Bennett
- INF-3511: audit log plumbing + immutable events (3) - owner: Priya Singh
- INF-3516: cost estimate microservice contract (2) - owner: Kenji Watanabe
- INF-3522: conflict-resolution UI + notifications (5) - owner: eng-sre pairing

Open questions for architecture / infra
- Do we want timeline events emitted by autoscaler synchronously, or should they be streamed from a separate event router? suggestion: stream via existing event-bus to keep UI latency low and avoid tight coupling.
- How to surface model-variant fallback suggestions? Add a short mapping table to the side panel from runtime.

Design tradeoffs considered (notes to PM and eng leads)
- Inline cost estimates keep the operator in context but increase number of calls; tradeoff: cache last known estimate and refresh on explicit changes.
- Optimistic UI for manual overrides reduces perceived latency but must be reconciled with eventual runtime responses. Implementation should mark optimistic states clearly.

Prototype notes (for next steps)
- I will create a small Figma frame (card + timeline + side panel) and record a 90s walkthrough demo for the sprint planning meeting.
- UX test: 5 engineers (SRE/product) simulate a 10-minute incident and use quick-burst and rollback flows. Capture time-to-resolution and error rates.

Appendix: quick grooming checklist for the sprint kickoff
- confirm acceptance criteria + owners (this doc)
- add backend contract for /events?limit=100 and /burst-request POST (validate)
- allocate 1 day for telemetry schema review with infra
- schedule 30m UX QA after first dev build

Notes to reviewers
- Look for clarity on 'convert burst to reservation' language and whether finance needs separate approval flow (I put it into 'soft block' for later).
- If we want reservations to be multi-region, we should call out UX for cross-pool mapping (future ticket).

Last quick sketch (verbal):
Pool card
[Pool: cv1-prod] [region: us-west1] [A100-v2]   [Pause autoscale] [Quick-burst]
KPIs: | GPU 72% (5m) | queued 12 | 95p 132ms | tokens 120k/m |
Timeline: |--autoscale+--burst--manual override--autoscale- |
Click marker -> Slide panel: Summary | Logs | Cost (est)

End.
